title: Scope service database credentials per ControlPlane
summary:
Security review of CC-0116 (per-ControlPlane Keystone DB credential scoping). All security-focus invariants hold. Per-tenant isolation is sound: dbCredentialRemoteKeyFor (reconcile_dbcredentials.go:37-39) embeds both {ns}/{name} so two ControlPlanes can never resolve to the same OpenBao DB-credential object; dbCredentialSecretName is name-only but the Secret/ExternalSecret lives in childNamespace(cp)=cp.Namespace (reconcile_infrastructure.go:44), so same-named CPs in different namespaces remain distinct namespace-scoped objects (the OpenBao remote key, the real shared-backend blast radius, always carries both axes). OpenBao policy changes are comment-only with no capability widening: eso-management.hcl keeps kv-v2/data/openstack/keystone/* read-only, eso-control-plane.hcl adds only a comment, the bootstrap seed at kv-v2/openstack/keystone/${cp_ns}/${cp_name}/db is deliberately NOT mark_eso_managed (read-only), and push-keystone-keys.hcl is unchanged and grants write only to fernet-keys/credential-keys (no .../db write). Secrets are never passed as cleartext CLI args nor logged: production bootstrap uses the in-pod @generate marker expanding to `bao write -field=random_bytes sys/tools/random/32` (write-bootstrap-secrets.sh:67-68), and reconcile_dbcredentials.go logs only Secret names and error strings (never secret values). The Owns(&esov1.ExternalSecret{}) watch (controlplane_controller.go:293) is CORRECT and not a dead watch: the operator creates the ExternalSecret and sets a controller owner reference of kind=ControlPlane (SetControllerReference at reconcile_dbcredentials.go:128), unlike ESO-materialised Secrets which carry ownerRef.kind=ExternalSecret and are handled via the separate field-indexer Watches(&Secret{}) mapper. No hardcoded production credentials; the condition-type const and Secret-name-suffix const both carry //nolint:gosec G101 false-positive markers (controlplane_controller.go:49, reconcile_dbcredentials.go:29). Managed mode correctly overrides keystone.Spec.Database.SecretRef to the operator-owned Secret only when ClusterRef != nil; brownfield is a true no-op leaving the user secretRef untouched (reconcile_keystone.go:118-121). No security issues found.

Quality review of CC-0116 (scope Keystone DB credentials per ControlPlane). The new reconcile_dbcredentials.go faithfully mirrors the established per-CR patterns: dbCredentialRemoteKeyFor copies adminAppCredentialRemoteKeyFor's ns+name OpenBao path scoping, and reconcileDBCredentials uses the exact CreateOrUpdate+SetControllerReference idiom from ensureAppCredentialSecret. Condition type/reasons, the requeue const (dbCredentialsRequeueAfter, matching korcRequeueAfter cadence with a documented rationale), the //nolint:gosec G101 discipline, and the dual condition-map registrations (subConditionTypes + subReconcilerConditionTypes) all follow existing conventions. The change is genuinely surgical: the keystone operator is byte-identical (empty diff main...HEAD -- operators/keystone/), reconcile_keystone.go adds only a managed-mode SecretRef substitution guarded by ClusterRef != nil (commonv1 already imported), and the only SetupWithManager change is the new Owns(&esov1.ExternalSecret{}) watch (mirrored in the envtest harness). Docs are thorough and accurate: the sub-reconciler count is updated 5->6 in every location, the DBCredentialsReady condition/reason table, projected-children table, metric-label table, OpenBao path-migration table, and vitepress sidebar all match the code; no live consumer references the legacy flat openstack/keystone/db path (remaining references are all migration notes, comments, cleanup docs, or the test's negative-assertion constant). The dbCredentialSecretName name-only choice (keystoneName(cp)+"-db-credentials") is documented as an explicit DECISION, is pattern-consistent with adminAppCredentialSecretName (also name-only), and is acceptable because the Secret is namespace-scoped while the OpenBao remote key (the actual shared-backend blast radius) embeds both namespace and name. Stage-b (dynamic DB engine / PushSecret) is correctly framed as deferred/not-implemented in the explanation doc. Test names accurately describe their coverage and the assertions back them up. Only two LOW documentation/comment nits found; nothing blocking.

Testing coverage for CC-0116 is broad and well-layered: unit tests (reconcile_dbcredentials_test.go) cover the scoping helpers (table-driven same-name/diff-ns and diff-name/same-ns), the ExternalSecret builder, the managed create+gate path, idempotency, brownfield no-op (two dedicated tests), the readiness wait (both branches), and the ensure-error path; reconcile_keystone_test.go adds dedicated managed-override and brownfield-untouched secretRef tests; instrumentation_test.go adds a belt-and-suspenders condition-registration test; setupwithmanager_test.go covers Owns(ExternalSecret); integration_test.go adds a real ordering-gate test (Consistently Keystone NotFound until the ES syncs) plus a multi-CP distinct-paths test. Assertions are generally specific (function-derived AND literal anchors, no tautological constants). The one substantive issue is an OVERCLAIMING unit test: TestCredentialInvariant_DriveChainIncludesDBCredentialsBeforeKeystone — its name and docstring assert it proves DBCredentials runs BEFORE Keystone, but both of its assertions (the ES exists/owned, and Keystone.Spec.Database.SecretRef == dbCredentialSecretName(cp)) hold regardless of ordering, because reconcileKeystone computes that secretRef name as a pure deterministic function of cp with no read of the ExternalSecret. The genuine ordering gate is the integration test; the unit test's name/comment overstate its coverage (ensure-test-names-accurately-describe-coverage). No tier is missing (helm-unittest legitimately N/A: the DB credential is operator-generated, not a chart template; the unchanged externalsecrets ClusterRole rule is already asserted per the baseline).

issues_found.description: The explanation doc cross-references numbered sections "§4" and "§5" (in the Migration bullets) but its headings are not numbered (e.g. '## Deferred: operator-owned PushSecret + `push-keystone-db.hcl`' and '## Stage-b: dynamic database secret engine'). A reader cannot resolve §4/§5 to a heading. Cosmetic only.
issues_found.fix: Either number the headings (## 4. Deferred..., ## 5. Stage-b...) or replace the "§4"/"§5" references with the heading titles (e.g. "the Deferred PushSecret section" / "the Stage-b section").

issues_found.description: The driveCredentialChain comment states the chain runs 'KORC -> AdminCredential -> Catalog -> DBCredentials -> Keystone', which diverges from the production order where DBCredentials runs BEFORE KORC (Infrastructure -> DBCredentials -> Keystone -> KORC -> AdminCredential -> Catalog). The comment correctly scopes its claim to the 'immediately BEFORE reconcileKeystone' sub-invariant so it is not technically wrong, but the stated chain order could mislead a reader into thinking production runs DBCredentials after Catalog. Worth a clarifying phrase that this is a test-only ordering preserving only the DBCredentials-immediately-before-Keystone invariant.
issues_found.fix: Append to the comment that this is a test-only chain order which intentionally differs from production (where DBCredentials precedes KORC) and only preserves the DBCredentials-immediately-before-Keystone gate the assertions rely on.

issues_found.description: TestCredentialInvariant_DriveChainIncludesDBCredentialsBeforeKeystone overclaims ORDERING. Its name and docstring assert it proves DBCredentials runs BEFORE Keystone ('which is only possible if DBCredentials ran before Keystone in the chain'), but neither of its two assertions actually distinguishes ordering. (1) The ES-existence/ownership check (es, ok := getDBCredentialES; OwnerReferences) only proves reconcileDBCredentials RAN at some point in the chain, not that it ran before reconcileKeystone. (2) The Keystone secretRef check k.Spec.Database.SecretRef.Name == dbCredentialSecretName(cp) is satisfied by reconcileKeystone ALONE: in managed mode reconcileKeystone sets keystone.Spec.Database.SecretRef = {Name: dbCredentialSecretName(cp), Key: "password"} as a pure deterministic function of cp (reconcile_keystone.go:121-122), with NO read of the ExternalSecret. If driveCredentialChain were reordered to call reconcileKeystone before reconcileDBCredentials, both assertions would still pass — so the test cannot detect the very regression its name promises. The real ordering gate is the integration test TestIntegration_FullReconcile_DBCredentialsBeforeKeystone (Consistently Keystone NotFound until the ES syncs). The unit test is still useful as a chain-wiring/secretRef-consumption check, but the name and docstring should be corrected to not claim it proves ordering.
issues_found.fix: Rename to reflect what it actually verifies (e.g. TestCredentialInvariant_DriveChainProjectsKeystoneAgainstDBCredentialSecret) and amend the docstring/inline comments at lines 310-317 and 338-339 to drop the 'only possible if DBCredentials ran before Keystone' ordering claim, instead pointing to TestIntegration_FullReconcile_DBCredentialsBeforeKeystone as the authoritative ordering proof. No production-code change needed.

suggested_improvements: tests/e2e/c5c3/db-credential-scoping/chainsaw-test.yaml:240 seeds a hardcoded dummy password literal `password=keystone-db-pw` as a `bao kv put` CLI arg against the ephemeral kind cluster. This is acceptable for a test fixture (no production credential, ephemeral backend, mirrors the existing multi-controlplane chainsaw seed pattern) but for defence-in-depth consistency with write-bootstrap-secrets.sh you could seed via an in-pod `bao write -field=random_bytes` generation so no cleartext appears in the kubectl-exec arg/process list even in CI logs. LOW / informational only — not a blocker.

Consider extracting a shared per-CR ExternalSecret-builder helper if a third per-CP read-only ExternalSecret is ever added; today two instances (admin clouds.yaml read ES via PushSecret family + this DB-credential ES) do not yet justify the abstraction (YAGNI-correct as-is).
Optionally add a CI grep-gate asserting no live manifest references the flat `openstack/keystone/db\b` path, to prevent regressions; the facts confirm none exists today but nothing enforces it.

TestIntegration_FullReconcile_DBCredentialsBeforeKeystone uses a 2s Consistently window (line 692-693) while dbCredentialsRequeueAfter is 10s; the watch-triggered re-reconcile from the ES Create keeps Keystone absent, so the assertion holds, but a brief comment noting that the Owns(ExternalSecret) watch re-fires within the window (rather than relying solely on the 10s requeue) would make the non-vacuousness explicit to future maintainers.

Consider one negative integration assertion that the brownfield managed-vs-brownfield branch leaves Keystone.Spec.Database.SecretRef untouched end-to-end (currently brownfield secretRef behavior is unit-only via TestReconcileKeystone_BrownfieldDBSecretRefUntouched); not required, the unit coverage is adequate.
next_steps: None required for the security focus. Stage-b PushSecret + dynamic database secret engine (which introduces the first write grant over a .../db path) must be re-reviewed for least-privilege when implemented, per the deferred design in docs/explanation/c5c3/db-credential-scoping.md.
Optionally apply the two LOW doc/comment clarifications (both AUTO_FIX, non-blocking).
No code changes required; quality gate passes.

Decide whether to rename/retag TestCredentialInvariant_DriveChainIncludesDBCredentialsBeforeKeystone and correct its docstring (ASK — purely a test-naming/comment accuracy change, no behavior change).
